text:
ConocoPhillips rose a modest 0.28% today, holding near $135 after bouncing back from a sharp drop earlier this week. The stock had fallen about 3% from November 18th to November 23rd, likely tracking the broader weakness in oil prices—US crude fell to the mid-$70s range before recovering to $82 today, while global Brent crude sits at nearly $93. The slight gain today reflects stabilization in energy markets rather than any company-specific catalyst.

The collapse of climate negotiations at COP31, which failed to commit governments to phasing out fossil fuels, may have provided some relief to energy investors worried about regulatory headwinds. At the same time, Wall Street analysts have continued to highlight dividend-paying energy stocks as attractive income plays, which could be supporting the stock's recovery from its recent lows.
